papers.title: The modified spacer for first stage revision hip arthroplasty
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND Periprosthetic infection following total hip arthroplasty usually necessitates a single or two-stage revision procedure. Loose cement should be removed but removal of well fixed cement risks complications and can potentially be left. When adopting a two-stage strategy, either an excision arthroplasty is performed or following debridement, an antibiotic impregnated spacer is implanted. Cement spacers may fracture (Fig 1), resulting in limb shortening and a less functional joint. We describe a simple technique that strengthens the spacer, thereby preventing fracture.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文仅讨论髋关节翻修术中抗生素骨水泥间隔器的改良技术，未涉及股骨假体应力遮挡、微动或有限元分析。
llm.why_not_core: This paper is a clinical surgical technique report on spacer modification for periprosthetic infection; it contains no biomechanics modeling, no FEA, no implant stress analysis, no micromotion quantification, and no patient-specific computational analysis.

summary_en.motivation: To prevent fracture of antibiotic-impregnated cement spacers used in two-stage revision hip arthroplasty.
summary_en.method: A simple reinforcement technique for the cement spacer is described without computational or experimental mechanical testing.
summary_en.result: The strengthened spacer theoretically reduces fracture risk, though no quantitative evidence is provided.
summary_en.validation: No mechanical testing, FEA, or clinical outcome data are presented; the paper is purely descriptive.
